sections.heading: How to Play Restoration
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Restoration"][color=druid]Restoration Druid Rotation in Midnight[/color][/h2]
[pad]
Restoration Druid is a heal-over-time-based healer that combines such effects with a large direct heal that scales off them in [spell=8936]. Restoration Druid has many answers to most questions dungeons will ask of you and you should feel like a very powerful healer once you've picked up the basics. It is especially well-suited to small group content. In Midnight, it largely plays similarly to previous expansions. Here are a few quick tips to get you started:

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=inv_relics_idolofrejuvenation size=medium type=round color=c11 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=druid]Swiftmend Casts:[/color][/b] [spell=18562] has a ton of extra effects attached to it which makes even 100% overheal casts very high value. Such effects include [spell=102693], [spell=392356], Everbloom, [spell=440118] and more. 
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_druid_empoweredrejuvination size=medium type=round color=c11 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=druid]Utilize [spell=207383]:[/color][/b] Put [spell=774] out on the group before or as damage hits so that your follow-up [spell=8936] casts are cheap with a high Crit chance. This is the heart of the Restoration Druid playstyle and most of our healing and mana efficiency starts here.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_ardenweald_druid size=medium type=round color=c11 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=druid]Use Major Cooldowns:[/color][/b] Cast [spell=323764] / [spell=33891] and [spell=740] very often. Pre-plan them before tough fights so that you can line them up with difficult moments in the fight. [/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]

[center][wrapper width=800px][box border=true]If you're looking for a more bite-sized rotation explanation, check out our simplified guide below:

[center][cta-button=guide=32654 icon=spell_nature_healingtouch]Restoration Druid Beginner Guide[/cta-button][/center][/box][/wrapper][/center]

sections.heading: Wildstalker Raid
sections.body:
[h2 toc=false type=bar][icon name=spell_lifegivingseed  size=medium type=round color=c11 inline=true][/icon] [color=druid]Wildstalker Raid[/color][/h2]
[/div]
[wrapper width=850px]

[pad]

[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/1293669.png]
The Druid raid strategy focuses on [b][color=orange-gem]two key components[/color][/b]:

[h3 type=bar]Everbloom[/h3]
[rotation-timeline]
[rt-step=33763 text="Self"]
[rt-step=774 text="Self x2"]
[rt-step=18562 text="On CD, On Self"]
[/rotation-timeline]
Maintain [spell=33763] on yourself, alongside multiple heal-over-time effects like 2x [spell=774]s. [spell=18562] yourself on cooldown. You will also maintain a [spell=8936] HoT on yourself but this will happen automatically via the [spell=278515] talent. We are doing all of this to maximize our Everbloom healing.

[b]Extra Tips[/b]
[ul][li]You can refresh any HoT that is nearly expired (less than ~5-6 seconds left) with no penalty.[/li]
[/ul]

[toggler id=everbloomE hidden]Explain Why[/toggler]
[div id=everbloomE hidden]
[pad]
Your Apex talent, Everbloom, does a lot of AoE healing whenever your lifebloom "blooms". This healing scales with the number of heal-over-time effects on the lifebloom target via our Mastery (Mastery: Harmony). The [spell=33763] itself will bloom about 4 times a minute (whenever you refresh it close to its expiry). That's not much healing so we have two ways of getting more:
[ul]
[li]The [spell=274902] talent gives all HoTs on the target an 8% chance of causing a bloom. [b]This is reason two to stack the target with HoTs.[/b][/li]
[li]Whenever we press [spell=18562], [spell=33763] will "bloom" 3 times in a row. [spell=18562] will also put a [spell=439530] on the target increasing all healing received (and thus splashed) via [spell=440118]. Another reason to press [spell=18562] as many times as possible.[/li]
[/ul]

To recap, we stack HoTs on the [spell=33763] target to proc [spell=274902] more, and to increase the amount of healing they do. 
[/div]
[pad]
[pad]
[toggler id=everbloomimprove]How to Improve at this[/toggler]
[div id=everbloomimprove hidden]
[pad]
To improve at any World of Warcraft spec, you should get comfortable with using Warcraftlogs. [url=https://www.warcraftlogs.com/help/start]There is an introduction to it here.[/url] A log will give you a ton of information about how you played, and will help you improve by giving you access to concrete information on what errors you are making.

Once you have a log of a fight, you can select to view buffs on yourself in the "Buffs" tab.
[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/1293672.png]

Scroll down to check the uptime on [spell=33763], [spell=774], [spell=774] ([spell=155675]) and [spell=8936]. Your general goal is to be at 90%+ on all of these - particularly [spell=33763] which should be at 100%. 

[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/1293674.png]
Do not expect perfect play right away, but track this and look to improve a little bit each raid. 

[/div]


[h3 type=bar]Abundance[/h3]
[rotation-timeline]
[rt-step=774 text="5x"]
[rt-step=207383 text="Activates"]
[rt-step=8936 text="Spam"]
[rt-step=774 text="Repeat"]
[/rotation-timeline]
Maintain the [spell=207383] buff by keeping five [spell=774] buffs active. Then casting [spell=8936] to take advantage. Track this on your UI. When the fight ends you should have many more [spell=8936] casts than [spell=774] casts.

[b]Extra Tips[/b]
[ul][li]It is better to batch the [spell=774] casts together rather than casting them one by one. [/li]
[li]Pressing [spell=18562] before [spell=774] will cause your next cast to spread three HoTs instead of one. This is a great way of keeping [spell=207383] active for little time investment.[/li]
[/ul]

[toggler id=abundanceE]Explain Why[/toggler]
[pad]
[div id=abundanceE hidden]
With [spell=207383] active, [spell=8936] becomes your most efficient spell cast due to the massive mana cost reduction it offers. [b][color=druid]Almost all players will do more HPS by casting fewer [spell=774]s and more [spell=8936]s.[/color][/b]
[/div]
[br]

[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/1293671.png]
[h3 type=bar]Wild Growth, Nature's Swiftness and Wrath[/h3]
[spell=48438] is a high-HPS, high-cost spell that you should push whenever the raid is in danger. It is your primary mana throttle so if you are running out, then consider cutting [spell=48438] casts - particularly from moments of the fight that aren't as dangerous. [b]Avoid generically casting it whenever it's available.[/b]

[spell=132158] greatly increases the healing of your next [spell=8936] and is on a medium cooldown. With the [spell=203651] talent, self-cast this during dangerous or semi-dangerous damage. It will automatically refresh the HoTs on yourself, heal your other [spell=8936] targets for a lot (via [spell=1263879]), and will proc a lot of [spell=274902] over the next 10 seconds. Fantastic value.

[spell=5176] is a damage spell that will also regenerate mana via the [spell=289237] talent. This will unlock more mana to spend on expensive spells like [spell=48438]. Cast it during downtime. If damage is persistently heavy and there's no downtime then you are better off waiting for [spell=207383] to drop before you spam [spell=5176] since it's much more efficient than casting it mid-[spell=207383] cycle.



[/wrapper]
[/tab]
[tab name="Mythic+ Healing" icon=ability_druid_rescue]
[pad]
[wrapper width=850px]
[pad]

In dungeon content, you will heal a combination of unavoidable and avoidable damage. The former you will be expected to heal through, the latter you will do what you can but ultimately aren't always responsible for. Restoration brings significant healing in Mythic+, which means you can heal through more mistakes than most other specs. Let's look at the healing abilities available to us:


[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/1232931.png alt="General Healing"]

[table][tr][td]
[rotation-timeline]
[rt-step=81262 text="Active"]
[rt-step=33763 text="Active"]
[rt-step=18562 text="On CD"]
[rt-step=48438 text="Often"]
[/rotation-timeline]
[/td][/tr][/table]


[ol class=entity-list id=healing-rotation]
[li]Keep [spell=81262] active at all times. If you are running [spell=1217941] (and the default build does) then keeping [spell=33763] up does this for you. [span class=tip tooltip=[spell=1217941][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
4[li]Keep [spell=33763] up at all times. This is [b]crucial[/b] and [spell=33763] will make up a lot of your dungeon healing via our Apex, Everbloom. [span class=tip tooltip=[spell=33763]Refresh[symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li]Cast [spell=18562] on cooldown, even if the party is reasonably healthy. It'll proc [spell=392302] which will put out two [spell=774]s. You have a second charge for burst healing anyway.[/li]
2[li]Cast [spell=48438] during moderate damage periods, or to top the group up after minor damage. It's extremely GCD efficient, and also adds a Mastery stack to everyone in your group.[/li]
6[li]React to anyone dropping very low with [spell=132158] + [spell=8936], or just [spell=8936] depending on what is available.[/li]
7[li]Fill any free time by contributing DPS. We'll cover that in detail below.[/li]
[/ol]

[h4 type=bar]Breakdown & Explanation[/h4]
Your key takeaway should be to take care of your maintenance tasks at all times (cooldown usage and uptimes mentioned above), and then use [spell=8936] as your primary healing button when people take damage. If you have time it's best to cast [spell=774] on a few people prior to damage to make the group safer but this is very dependent on the scenario you find yourself in. Let's look through a few common dungeon scenarios.


[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/1232932.png]
Mythic+ often has a lot of short bursts that you'll have to handle as the Healer. Abilities like Alerting Shrill in Ara-kara where the damage is sharp and occurs over 3-6 seconds. These abilities are very telegraphed, so you'll know they're coming and have an opportunity to prep for them. Consider the following advice when countering them, and note that you'll only get 2-3 casts inside the actual damage windows:
[ul][li]Start prepping your party for the damage 5-6 seconds in advance. Eventually, as you grow more confident, you'll get away with committing fewer GCDs to each big damage event, but when starting out, play safe. Make sure [spell=81262] is down, and that [spell=33763][color=q]s[/color] is active.[/li]
[li]Continue prepping by putting [spell=774] on the group, prioritizing your DPS since Tanks aren't often phased by this type of AoE damage.[/li]
[li]Cast [spell=48438] as the boss begins its cast.[/li]
[li]With [spell=33763] on allies A, cast [spell=18562] on B, and then cast [spell=8936] on whoever is most injured. Follow with further [spell=8936] casts to stabilize the group's Health.[/li]
[/ul]

[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/1232933.png]
You'll also have to handle a range of different, dangerous DoTs, but this section can also extend to Tank damage. With some mechanics, you'll get a few seconds to prepare but that's not guaranteed. If you're in a section of the dungeon with these, then it is worth keeping [spell=33763][color=q][/color] and [spell=81262] active the entire pull. 
[ul][li]Cast 1-2 [spell=774] on the target. It's not usually worth moving [spell=33763] to a target since you'll lose all 3 stacks.[/li]
[li]As the damage starts to tick, cast [spell=18562] followed by [spell=8936].[/li]
[li]Follow up with more [spell=8936]s, and use [spell=132158] if required.[/li]
[/ul]



[/wrapper]

[/tab]
[tab name="Pre-Combat Checks" icon=inv_misc_paperbundle02b]
[wrapper width=850px]
[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/1265740.png]
Here's what you should do before every raid or dungeon:
[ul][li]Cast [spell=1126] (our raid buff) - every pull.[/li]
[li]Make sure [spell=474750] is active on another player. Any squishy DPS player is a fine choice.[/li]
[li]Make sure you have a Flask on - applied every 1-2 hours.[/li]
[li]Make sure you have a Food buff - either every pull or every hour depending on the food.[/li]
[li]Make sure you have a [item=243734] on your weapon - applied every two hours.[/li]
[li](Optional) Make sure you have a [item=259085] on - every pull.[/li]
[li]Start casting [spell=774] a few seconds before the fight begins if there is relevant damage at the start. [/li]
[/ul]

You can read about the best Flask and food buff to use in the [url guide=3125]Restoration Consumables guide[/url].

[/wrapper]
[/tab]

[/tabs]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=druid][icon name=spell_nature_tranquility type=round size=medium inline=true color=c11][/icon] Restoration Druid Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]
Restoration has access to some of the most powerful healing cooldowns in the game. Let's go through them and discuss where we might use them. Aim to pre-plan cooldowns as often as possible. [b]Avoid scenarios where you're saving them "just in case"[/b], since this can cost you a lot of Mana through a fight and will increase the chance your raid suffers a death. Layer your raid's defensive cooldowns over the most dangerous moments of each fight to ensure you're covered.
[pad]
[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Tranquility" icon=spell_nature_tranquility]
[wrapper width=850px]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=spell_nature_tranquility type=round size=medium inline=true color=c11][/icon][color=druid] Tranquility [/color][/h3]
[spell=740] is our most powerful healing cooldown. It heals the entire raid or group for a significant amount and then extends all HoTs on each target by 2 seconds per [spell=740] tick (10s overall - via the [spell=197721] talent). You'll want to line up [spell=740] with the most dangerous moments of the fight. You might even be assigned to use it at specific moments.

Playstyle-wise, you will want to change how you play in the lead-up to using [spell=740]. Because the extension mechanic is so powerful, we'll want to maximize how many effects we're extending. The most valuable heal-over-time effect to extend is actually [spell=8936]. It'll look a little something like this:


[table][tr][td]
We have one key ramp sequence remaining in the rotation. [spell=740] extends all of our HoTs, so we will want to structure our gameplay going into it. Start this about 15-20 seconds before your [spell=740] is assigned:
[rotation-timeline]

[rt-step=18562]
[rt-step=774 text="3x"]
[rt-step=8936 text="Many"]
[rt-step=18562]
[rt-step=8936]
[rt-step=48438]
[rt-step=740]
[rt-step=8936 text="As many as you need"]
[/rotation-timeline]
[/td][/tr][/table]

We will put out a [spell=48438] and as many [spell=8936] buffs as possible, then extend them with [spell=740]. This gives us a wide window to cast [spell=8936]s afterwards and because we extended a lot of [spell=8936] HoTs too, these casts will all splash to them via [spell=1263879]. This is about a 20-25s window of healing in total and it is one of the biggest healing cooldowns in the game. If you take [spell=33891] then it's often worth combining it with [spell=740] because it'll actually pause the duration of your tree buff while you channel.

In Dungeons, [spell=740] is used more for the healing it does by itself rather than its ramp / combo potential. Use it whenever the group is in danger.

[/wrapper]
[/tab]
[tab name="Convoke the Spirits" icon=inv_ability_druid_convokethespirits]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=inv_ability_druid_convokethespirits type=round size=medium inline=true color=c11][/icon][color=druid] Convoke the Spirits [/color][/h3]
[wrapper width=850px]
[spell=323764] is a unique ability that casts 12-16 Druid abilities at random targets. The spells chosen have some logic to them but will mostly feel random. You can roughly expect:
[ul]
[li]0-2 [spell=48438] casts[/li]
[li]2-4 [spell=18562] casts[/li]
[li]4-5 non-resto casts like [spell=5176][/li]
[li]A handful of [spell=774] and [spell=8936][/li]
[li]A 50% chance of casting a single-tick-[spell=740] (if you have the [spell=393371] talent - this procs a two-second HoT extension as well if you have [spell=197721]).[/li]
[/ul]

Convoke will also change its spells if you cast it in a different [i]form[/i]. In [spell=768] you will mostly get Cat-abilities, in [spell=24858] balance-abilities and so on. 

[h4]How to use it[/h4]
In raid, we will always cast it in our regular caster form. We'll want to cast [spell=48438] beforehand, since if we get the [spell=197721]-extension then we'd like to get as much value out of that as possible. Our Convoke casts are no longer big healing moments, and you should look to maximize the number of useful casts you get over a fight.

In Mythic+, we'll cast Convoke in caster form if we need healing, and in [spell=768] if we want to contribute more DPS. Its low cooldown gives us a lot of flexibility in our usage!


[/wrapper]
[/tab]
[tab name="Incarnation: Tree of Life" icon=ability_druid_improvedtreeform]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_druid_improvedtreeform type=round size=medium inline=true color=c11][/icon][color=druid] Incarnation: Tree of Life [/color][/h3]
[wrapper width=850px]
Incarnation is our alternative to [spell=323764] and it focuses around increasing your healing for a longer period of time since Incarnation lasts a massive 30 seconds. You also get cooldown reduction for every Grove Guardian dropped so while it'll always be a longer cooldown than [spell=323764], you can cast it about every 1:40 with good play. If you take [spell=392356] too then you can end up with 60-70% Incarnation uptime!

[spell=33891] gives the following benefits while active, and any [spell=774]s you had out before you cast Incarnation will also benefit:
[ul]
[li]All healing increased by 10%.[/li]
[li][spell=774] healing increased by 40%. Mana cost reduced by 30%.[/li]
[li][spell=48438] hits 2 additional targets.[/li]
[li][spell=5176] damage increased by 20%.[/li]
[li][spell=8936] is now instant-cast.[/li]
[/ul]

That's a decent package of power overall - particularly to [spell=774]. You might take [spell=33891] if a fight is very high on movement since while casting [spell=8936] is not an HPS increase, it does allow you to cast it while on the move.

[h4]How to use it[/h4]
You'll generally want to use Incarnation 10-12 seconds before major damage hits. That way you can take advantage of the massive discount to [spell=774]. You can otherwise do your standard rotation while Incarnation is active. Note that its duration is paused while you're channeling [spell=740] and combining the two is a good idea.
[/wrapper]
[/tab]

[/tabs]

sections.heading: Druid Deep Dives
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Druid Deep Dives" type=bar][icon name=spell_nature_healingtouch color=c11 inline=true size=medium type=round][/icon] Druid Deep Dives[/h2]
In this section, we'll cover different aspects of the spec in a little more depth. These are optional reads, but can be useful in increasing your overall understanding of the class. If you're brand new to the spec, I'd recommend getting some practice in first and then revisiting.
[br]

[tabs name="Deep Dives"]
[tab name="Catweaving"]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_druid_catform type=round size=medium inline=true color=c11][/icon][color=druid] Catweaving [/color][/h3]
[wrapper width=850px]
Catweaving is a way for us to contribute DPS where we swap to our [spell=768] shapeshift and cast [spell=768] abilities like [spell=1822] and [spell=1079]. It tends to be the highest DPS playstyle available to us in both raid and Mythic+, but it has a bit more complexity than just pressing [spell=5176] with downtime so it gets its own section instead. You can generally master Restoration Druid [i]healing[/i] first, and then start to incorporate Cat-gameplay once you're comfortable with the spec. 

[b]Your DPS is not that important. At all times, make sure the party is comfortable first.[/b]

[ul]
[li]Cast [spell=5215] before combat to get into stealth. This will also greatly buff our first ability cast.[/li]
[li]Open with a [spell=1822] on the highest health enemy.[/li]
[li]Continue applying rake to different enemies in the pack. When you have 5 combo points press [spell=1079] instead.[/li]
[li]Once everyone has [spell=1822], cast [spell=106785] (3+ targets) or [spell=5221] (1-2 targets) instead.[/li]
[li]On a single target, cast [spell=22568] instead of [spell=1079] if the target already has one. [/li]
[/ul]

Catweaving really boils down to "Apply [spell=1822] and [spell=1079] to as many targets as you can". You will want to have [spell=1822] (and optionally [spell=5221]) on your caster-form bar since that'll let you enter [spell=768] automatically without spending a global cooldown (via [spell=449193]). This also makes the playstyle flow much better.
[/wrapper]
[/tab]
[/tabs]

[hr]
Our Restoration Druid guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on [b]View Changelog[/b] in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Restoration Druid guides for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b], make sure to browse the [i]Navigation Bar[/i] at the top of the page.
[pad]


[pad]
[hr]

sections.heading: Feedback
sections.body:
[h2 toc=false]Feedback[/h2]

Thanks for reading our class guides! If you have any feedback, feel free to leave a comment in the section below, and we will reply as quickly as possible.
